key_insight: Re-Search turns research ideation into a Twenty Questions–style game: an LLM asks yes-or-no questions to rediscover a published paper’s core idea. This makes the model’s step-by-step search process visible rather than evaluating only its final proposal.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations obscure how LLMs explore and refine research ideas, making it difficult to identify what limits their progress.
method: Give the model only the research problem from a published paper.
Let it ask yes-or-no questions to narrow down possible approaches and rediscover the paper’s core idea.
Examine the questioning trajectory to study how the model explores ideas and uses feedback.
impact: The framework could help practitioners diagnose weaknesses in LLM-driven research ideation and design better feedback strategies. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so it does not establish performance results.
visual_elements: Two-player diagram showing an LLM asking questions and a respondent providing yes-or-no feedback.
Branching decision tree illustrating how answers narrow the space of research ideas.
Step-by-step path from a research problem to a rediscovered core idea.
Side-by-side comparison of final-answer evaluation and search-process evaluation.
paper_title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
paper_authors: Muhan Gao, Hangxiao Zhu, Xinqi Su, Yu Zhang, Daniel Khashabi
